title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
AI-generated deepfakes and fake videos enabled criminals to impersonate a real immigration attorney at scale across social media platforms. Scammers deployed hundreds of fraudulent accounts using the attorney's identity to solicit payments from vulnerable immigrants seeking legal services, directing victims through social media to off-platform payment methods.

The failure occurred in the deployment phase of the AI systems themselves. The deepfake technology was not built with identity verification safeguards, nor were the social media platforms enforcing sufficient authentication checks to prevent accounts from impersonating real professionals before victims had already been defrauded. Detection happened only after the attorney received calls from victims who had already lost money.

It is not established how the criminals obtained the attorney's likeness, nor whether the platform takedowns succeeded in eliminating the fraud entirely rather than simply removing visible accounts.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of sophisticated AI-generated scams targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using artificial intelligence to impersonate Leal, offering fraudulent immigration services he never provides. In one scheme, scammers use deepfake videos to promise US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200 cash payments. Leal first discovered the fraud when potential clients began calling his office after seeing these fake videos online.

The situation has escalated dramatically over the past three months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company to combat the fraud. The company has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Scammers typically direct victims through social media to WhatsApp numbers, then send phony contracts and request payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams and is warning immigrants to verify identities of anyone offering legal services online and avoid paying through digital payment apps.
